newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Arthur C. Clarke launches latest book - "3001".
newsitem.headline: Arthur C. Clarke launches latest book - "3001".

text.p: Space visionary Arthur C. Clarke announced on Thursday the global launch of his latest book "3001: The Final Odyssey".
The novel is the final of Clarke's popular science fiction series which began with his 1968 classic "2001: A Space Odyssey".
Clarke, 79, shared an Oscar nomination with Stanley Kubrick for the screenplay of the film by the same name that year.
Of the two literary sequels "2010" and "2061", the former was also made into a film.
At Thursday's launch, held at the British Council in Colombo, a chapter of the novel was read aloud by a member of the audience and Clarke later signed copies of the book.
In "3001", the perfectly preserved body of Clarke's hero Frank Poole, which has drifted in space for 1,000 years, is retrieved by Captain Dimitri Chandler of the spacetug Goliath.

Medical and electro-optical technologies bring Poole back to life and he is then enhanced with a Braincap. Poole thus becomes a telepathic, machine-assisted inhabitant of the first years of the fourth mellennium, with a lot to learn.
Earlier on Thursday, Clarke unveiled a bust of himself at Colombo's 130-year-old Galle Face Hotel, where he said much of "3001" was written.

Speaking at the hotel, he predicted that petroleum products would be replaced by the end of the century by other forms of energy and looking at his glass of orange juice, added: "The amount of energy in a glass of orange juice is infinite and we will be able to tap it".
The British-born Clarke, who has also scores of non-fiction books, has been living in Sri Lanka for the past 30 years.
